 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  8.A  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC-2022-042; A Resolution of the
  Planning Commission of the City of Palmdale, approving Conditional Use Permit 22-
  010; a request to establish a Type 47 (beer, wine, and distilled spirits)
  Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control license for a bona fide restaurant located
  at 1205 West Rancho Vista Boulevard (Pier 88) and finding the project Categorically
  Exempt (Staff Reference: Assistant Planner Sam Dominguez)

  Commissioner Alvarez asked regarding the over intensification with the expectation
  of growth and concentration of alcohol licenses as mentioned in the staff report and
  asked for clarification on the numbers.

  Assistant Planner Dominguez clarified that the location of this establishment is in an
  area that has a higher number of alcohol licenses. The City uses two methods:
  Population Density is Method 1 – the ratio within the census tract is one for every 20
  and Citywide one for every 88 establishments. Retail Density is Method 2 – where
  the number of licenses is gathered from within a 2,500-foot radius of 20 randomly
  selected On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments located within commercial
  areas and compared to a 2,500-foot radius of the project site. Over intensification is
  common for this area since it is surrounding the AV Mall and the previous use at this
  location also held the same ABC license.

  Chair Nemeth opened the Public Hearing on this item.

  Applicant Brett Engstrom gave some basic information related to this location, and
  noted that this is the same license the previous restaurant held at this location. His
  staff will attend a training course offered by ABC and he will ensure his staff will
  practice safe sales of all alcoholic beverages.

  Chair Nemeth closed the Public Hearing on this item.

  Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-042 approving Conditional Use
  Permit 22-010 and find that the project is Categorically Exempt
  from environmental review.

PROJECT NO:  Conditional Use Permit 13-009 Major Modification

APPLICANT:  Baracoa Cuban Restaurant

PLANNER:  Sam Dominguez, Assistant Planner

DATE:  December 8, 2022

RECOMMENDATION

Adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-046 approving Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 13-009
Major Modification (MM), revoking previously approved CUP 15-010, and finding that the
project is Categorically Exempt from environmental review.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant is requesting to modify an existing Type 41 (Beer and Wine) Department
of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) license to a Type 47 (Beer, Wine, and Distilled
spirits) license to sell beer, wine, and distilled spirits within an existing 1,610 square foot
bona fide restaurant located at 853 Auto Center Drive, Suite F. The applicant has
requested that the Planning Commission consider the continued provision of live
entertainment consisting of a solo pianist, acoustical guitarist, small chamber ensemble,
or a musician on an occasional basis (no more than 12 days per month), which does not
occupy more than 50 square feet in floor area and does not include amplified sound. The
project does not include any expansion or exterior modification to the existing building or
associated parking area.

The on-site sale and consumption of alcohol is proposed to be incidental to the primary
restaurant operation. The alcoholic beverage component will utilize approximately
48 square feet or less than 10 percent [(48/1,610) x 100 = 3 percent] of the gross floor
area, for the sale, display, and storage of alcohol as depicted in Figure 3. All alcohol will
be stored in a secured location within a storage area and behind the bar for on-site
consumption only, as well as be displayed on a hanging shelf above the bar area.

The City recently adopted a comprehensive General Plan update. As such, the land use
designation for the site is EMPFX (Employment Flex); however, the exact uses allowed
within this designation and the development standards for future development will be
determined during a comprehensive update to the Zoning Ordinance, which is anticipated
to be completed in early 2023. As such, the project has been analyzed using the most
appropriate current zone, which is C-2 (Office Commercial). The bona fide restaurant is
permitted within the C-2 zone and incidental alcohol sales are allowable subject to
approval of a CUP application, as specified within Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC)
Sections 17.76.010 and 17.92.070.

BACKGROUND

On January 13, 2006, the existing medical office complex was approved by a hearing
officer through Site Plan Review (SPR) 8-05-1. On July 11, 2013, CUP 13-009
(Resolution No. PC-2013-022) was approved by the Planning Commission to establish
an on-sale alcoholic beverage establishment with a Type 41 ABC license within an
approximately 1,610 square foot tenant space for use as a restaurant (Baracoa Cuban
Restaurant). Subsequently, the City Council approved Entertainment Permit No. 13-18
(Resolution No. CC2014-002) on January 8, 2014, to allow for entertainment consisting

Public Convenience or Necessity

State law limits the number of alcohol licenses within each census tract, based on
population within the census tract area. Once the threshold is exceeded, which is often
referred to as undue concentration, the ABC will only issue additional licenses within the
applicable census tract if either the applicant demonstrates (for bona fide restaurants,
hotels, beer or wine manufacturers) or the local agency determines (for all other
establishments) that a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) will be served by the
additional license (Business and Professions Code Section 23958.4). In addition to
undue concentration, the ABC has the authority to deny an application for issuance of a
license that could potentially create a law enforcement problem (i.e. result in creation of
a high crime reporting district).

Undue Concentration

The proposed project is located within Census Tract 9102.18. Based upon information
provided by the ABC, in order to not exceed the countywide average of alcohol
establishments per resident, up to three on-sale licenses, may be issued (one per 1,000
residents). Currently, Census Tract 9102.18 has 23 existing on-sale licenses and 4,413
residents (2020 US Census). Therefore, there is an undue concentration of on-sale
licenses. As such, a PCN will be required by the ABC prior to issuance of an additional
license.

The undue concentration of on-sale licenses within the census tract is due to the small
number of residences (4,413) located in the census tract (6.5 square miles) as compared
to the large number of commercial uses and undeveloped commercial and industrial
land. The Employment Flex designation of the project site was established to permit
mixed-use development of lighter industrial uses and more intensive service, retail, and

High Crime Area

A high crime area is defined by PMC Section 17.16.080, as an area having a crime rate
of 120 percent or more of the average of the reporting districts within the City. According
to the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, there are 22 Crime Reporting Districts
(CRD) within the City of Palmdale, with a total of 7,443 Part I and Part II Crimes reported
for the year 2021. The average number of combined Part I and Part II Crime offenses for
the reporting period for all 22 districts was 338 (7,443 Part I and Part II Crimes/ 22 CRD),
and 20 percent greater than that average is 406 (338 x 1.20). The project is within CRD
2619 (Figure 5), which had a total of 688 Part I and Part II offenses, according to data
provided by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department. Therefore, the proposed use
is within a crime reporting area that exhibits a crime rate that is 204 percent
[(688 / 338) x 100] higher compared to all crime reporting districts across the City and is
considered to be in a high crime area.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided the most current location and
date information for Part I and Part II crimes reported for 2021. As shown on the 2021
Part I and Part II Crimes in CRD 2619 map (Figure 5), the crimes are scattered throughout
the reporting district.

Calls for Service

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided a summary of service calls and
crime history for the project site between September 21, 2021, to September 21, 2022.
The report indicates there has been two calls for service. The first call was for a vehicle
theft report, where the caller stated their vehicle was stolen from the parking lot while they
were eating dinner at the restaurant. The second call for service was for a burglary alarm.
According to the report, the location was checked and there were no indications of a
burglary.

After review of past service calls for the site, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department
has not indicated any opposition to the approval of this CUP. In addition, as specified
within the draft Conditions of Approval, if the proposed business generates an increase
in the number of calls for service, the Sheriff’s Department may request subsequent
review of the CUP by the City.

Surrounding Area

As specified within PMC Section 17.92.070.D, certain separations from alcohol uses to
sensitive uses are required, which are intended to ensure that such businesses are
located in a manner that avoids significant threats to public peace, health, safety, and
welfare. The project complies with all location standards because a review of the site
plan by the case planner revealed that no sexually oriented businesses exist within 1,000
feet of the bona fide restaurant. There are residences to the southwest of the site;
however, the Auto Center Drive and 10th Street West street intersection separates the
restaurant from the residences and acts as buffer for any threats to public peace, health,
safety, and welfare. In addition, there is a church on the parcel to the north (Faith
Community Church) and another church (Palmdale Methodist Church) on the parcel to
the west, across 10th Street West; however, there are no religious assembly separation
standards for bona fide restaurants per the PMC. The remainder of the uses in the vicinity
consist of medical offices, service uses, and other supportive uses. All activities occur
inside the restaurant within the hours of operation, the bar is incidental to the restaurant,
and the live entertainment will consist of unamplified music inside of the restaurant. As
such, the location is appropriate for this type of use.

Operations

The restaurant operates from 11:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and
11:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Friday and Saturday. The applicant will be required to comply
with all Conditions of Approval, restrictions of the ABC license, ABC regulations, and
reapply for a new ABC license should the use of the premises qualify for a different license
type. The sale, storage, and display of beer, wine and distilled spirits will utilize less than
10 percent of the floor area and is incidental to the primary restaurant use. In addition,
Conditions of Approval have been included within draft Resolution No. PC-2022-046
prohibiting the sale of alcohol for off-site consumption. Furthermore, the restaurant will
no longer include a dance floor, but will keep live entertainment that consists of a solo
pianist, acoustical guitarist, small chamber ensemble, or a musician on an occasional
basis (no more than 12 days per month), which does not occupy more than 50 square
feet in floor area and is not amplified.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) Guidelines review pursuant to Section 15301 of the CEQA Guidelines, which
exempts licensing of existing uses with negligible expansion of the use. The proposed
project will allow for a request to modify an existing Type 41 ABC license to a Type 47
ABC license for beer, wine and distilled spirits sales for on-site consumption within a bona
fide restaurant with occasional live entertainment, which is expected to be a negligible
expansion of the existing restaurant use.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request for the continued operation of an existing major wireless
telecommunications facility located at 38870 37th Street East for a period of 10 years.
The facility was previously approved as a 75-foot-high slimline monopole with an 875
square foot equipment enclosure.

BACKGROUND

On October 13, 2011, the Planning Commission approved CUP 11-016 (Resolution No.
PC-2011-045), which allowed for the construction of a 75-foot-high major wireless
telecommunications facility and an 875 square foot equipment enclosure.  On
November 13, 2014, the Planning Commission approved CUP 11-016 Major Modification
(Resolution No. PC-2014-041) for the installation of a second carrier and conversion of
the facility from a monopole to a mono-pine design; however, the modification was not
inaugurated and subsequently expired. As no time extension application has been
submitted for CUP 11-016, the entitlement expired on October 25, 2021.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.E.1, wireless facilities
expire in 10 years, unless a time extension is approved. Because a time extension
application was not received prior to expiration of the major wireless telecommunications
facility, the entitlement expired, and a new CUP is required for the continued operation of
the facility.

The existing facility has been modified twice since the original approval, through Minor
Modifications 18-001 and 19-029, approved on April 18, 2018, and February 26, 2019,
respectively.

Through the recent adoption of Palmdale 2045, a comprehensive General Plan Update,
the land use designation of this site has been changed to Employment Flex (EMPFX).
The approved project is consistent with the intent of the EMPFX designation; however,
as a complete, or substantially complete application was submitted prior to the
October 22, 2022, effective date of Palmdale 2045, this project will be evaluated based
on the previous land use designation and any applicable standards.

The subject application was initially submitted on August 1, 2022, and was deemed
incomplete. After resolution of completeness items, the application was deemed
complete and scheduled for the December 8, 2022, Planning Commission meeting.

Design

The existing major wireless telecommunications facility complies with the design
standards found within PMC Section 17.95.040.D.5. The monopole is painted gray, all
antennas are located within the radome, and the equipment is located within a neutral-
colored enclosure constructed of concrete masonry units. No advertising, signs, or
graphics are present on the existing structures.

Access

The existing site is within vacant area designated for future industrial development.
Access to the existing facility and equipment enclosure for maintenance purposes, will
continue to occur from 37th Street East, north of Avenue Q with only periodic trips to the
site for routine maintenance.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

An Initial Study was prepared for the project in conjunction with the original approval and
on October 13, 2011, the Planning Commission adopted an MND finding that, with the
incorporation of mitigation measures, the project would not have a significant impact on
the environment. Staff has reviewed the MND to determine whether the project triggered
any of the conditions described in Sections 15162, 15163, and 15164 of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines and determined that additional
documentation is not required for the project because CUP 22-012 does not propose any
significant revisions to the project, there are no changes in circumstances and there is no
new information of substantial importance that will involve new significant environmental
effects or increase the severity of previously identified significant effects. The proposed
project is a request to continue the operation of an existing major wireless
telecommunications facility and does not include any alterations to the major wireless
telecommunications facility as approved through CUP 11-016. Furthermore, an RF report
was submitted as part of the mitigation monitoring program and shows that the project
will continue to be compliant with FCC rules and regulations, as described in
OET Bulletin 65.

OPTIONS

The Planning Commission has the following options:

1.  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-045 approving CUP 22-012 and find that the
  project is consistent with the previously adopted MND and MMRP.

2.  Continue the project and direct staff to return with additional information.

3.  Deny the project.

Option 1 is recommended.

  The Electromagnetic Frequency reports submitted by the applicant
  demonstrate that the electronics radiation created by the facility will be
  within safe thresholds as determined by FCC standards. FCC regulations
  preempt local agencies from denying telecommunication facilities based
  upon perceived health impacts associated with EMF or RFR.

  Some members of the public have generated debate regarding the issue
  of health effects caused by electromagnetic energy used in wireless
  communications systems. The public’s concern revolves around whether
  the type of energy emitted by these systems affect humans and causes
  illnesses. There are three wireless communications sources that generate
  and use electromagnetic energy: Cell site antennas, hand-held portable
  communications devices, and electrical equipment in equipment buildings
  at cell sites and switching stations. Most scientists maintain that RFR and
  lower frequency EMFs, such as those associated with wireless
  communications systems, generally do not produce adverse health effects
  in humans because they are non-ionizing in nature and normal exposures

  are controlled so as not to result in thermal effects. Other researchers,
  however, note the possible molecular resonance problem described
  above, and propose that continuous low-level exposures in combination
  with other chemicals may cause health problems that are not immediately
  evident. These researchers suggest that extra care should be taken until
  more is known.

  The official guideline for facilities regulated by the Federal
  Communications Commission (FCC) is currently the American National
  Standards Institute (ANSI) guideline C95.1-2006. The ANSI guidelines
  recommend exposure limits covering RFR from 3 kHz (kilohertz) to 300
  GHz (gigahertz). The guidelines recognize that the human body absorbs
  radio frequency energy at some frequencies more readily than at others.
  The most restrictive limits are in the frequency range of 30-300 MHz.
  However, the wireless communications systems discussed herein operate
  in the frequency range of 870 to 2600 MHZ - frequencies outside of the
  most sensitive range. Based on this information, the potential for risks on

  The applicant has provided an initial EMF analysis that demonstrates that

  with ambient EMF sources, is within safe human thresholds. This
  requirement is made a mitigation measure for the project.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant is requesting to establish Type 21 (Off-Sale General) and Type 86
(Instructional On-Site Tasting) Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) licenses
to sell beer, wine, and spirits, and provide on-site tasting within a new grocery store. The
use will be located within an approved 38,105 square foot commercial building located at
the northwest corner of Rancho Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West. The proposed
alcohol use does not include any expansion or modification to the approved building or
parking area. Due to the location of the site, a Determination of Public Necessity is also
required to establish the proposed use.

The approval of CUP 22-015 will allow for the sale and on-site tasting of beer, wine, and
spirits as an incidental use within the grocery store. The alcoholic beverage component
will utilize approximately 1,140 square feet or less than 10 percent [(1,140/38,105) x 100
= 3 percent] of the gross floor area, for the sale, display, storage, or consumption of
alcohol as depicted in Figure 3. Additionally, approximately 150 square feet of the 1,140
square feet will only be used during tasting events.

BACKGROUND

The project was originally approved by the Planning Commission on July 11, 2019,
through Resolution No. PC-2019-027 for Planned Development (PD) 19-001,
Tentative Tract Map (TTM) 82636, Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 19-002, and Site Plan
Review (SPR) 19-003 for the development of a mixed-use project. On August 6, 2019,
the City Council approved General Plan Amendment (GPA) 19-001 and Zone Change
(ZC) 19-001 through Resolution No. CC-2019-068 in conjunction with the above
approvals. Following approval of the development, applications were approved by the
Planning Commission on May 13, 2021, through Resolution No. PC-2021-012, to phase
the subdivision of the site through TTM 82636 Major Modification. In addition, the
commercial portion of the project has been modified through Minor Modifications 19-075,
21-036, and 21-066, and the residential portion through Minor Modification 22-018.

GPA 19-001 and ZC 19-001 approved changes to the land use designation and zone to
accommodate the residential components of the project, PD 19-001 allowed flexibility of
development standards, TTM 82636 and TTM 82636 Major Modification approved the
subdivision and phasing of lots, and CUP 19-002 allowed the sale of beer and wine
(Alcoholic Beverage Control License Type 20 – Off-sale Beer and Wine) within a
proposed grocery store in the commercial component of the site.

Public Convenience or Necessity

According to State Law (§23817.7 and 23958.4 of the California Business and
Professions Code), all alcoholic beverage sales resulting in or adding to an undue
concentration of liquor licenses shall be subject to a determination that the public
convenience or necessity will be served by the issuance of the liquor license. State law
limits the number of alcohol licenses within each census tract, based on population within
the census tract area. Once the threshold is exceeded, which is often referred to as
undue concentration, the ABC will only issue additional licenses within the applicable
census tract upon a determination that Public Convenience or Necessity will be served
by the additional license. If the City does not make a determination within 90 days, the
ABC may do so instead. In addition to undue concentration, the ABC has the authority
to deny an application for issuance of a license that could potentially create a law
enforcement problem (i.e. result in creation of a high crime reporting district).

Undue Concentration

The proposed project is located within Census Tract 9102.14 (Figure 4). Based upon
information provided by the ABC, to not exceed the countywide average of alcohol
establishments for every resident, up to six on-sale and three off-sale licenses may be
issued. Currently, Census Tract 9102.14 has no existing on- or off-sale licenses.
Therefore, the district does not experience an undue concentration of alcohol licenses.

Crime Rate

A high crime area is defined by PMC Section 17.16.080, as an area having a crime rate
of 120 percent or more of the average of the reporting districts within the City. A total of
7,443 Part I and Part II crimes were reported within the City during 2021. The project is
within Crime Reporting District 2612, which had a total of 524 offenses during this period.
The average number of offenses for the reporting period for all 22 districts was 338 and
20 percent greater than that average would be 406. Therefore, the proposed use is within
a crime reporting area that exhibits a crime rate that is 155 percent of the citywide
average. As such, a Determination of Public Convenience or Necessity is required for a
high crime area.

Calls for Service

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided a summary of service calls and
crime history for the project site between August 18, 2021, to August 18, 2022, and the
report indicates there have been 18 calls for service in the vicinity. Nine of the calls were
traffic related incidents within the intersection, five calls were requests to check the
vicinity, two calls were regarding the same vandalism incident, one call was regarding a
suspicious person, and one call was for a disturbance. After review of past service calls
within CRD 2612, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department has not indicated any
opposition to the approval of this CUP. In addition, as specified within the draft Conditions
of Approval, if the proposed business generates an increase in the number of calls for
service, the Sheriff’s Department may request subsequent review of the CUP by the
Planning Commission.

Surrounding Area

As specified within PMC Section 17.92.070.D, certain separations from alcohol uses to
sensitive uses are required, which are intended to ensure that such businesses are
located in a manner that avoids significant threats to public peace, health, safety, and
welfare. The project complies with all location standards for incidental off-sale alcoholic
beverage establishments. In addition, the project complies with all location standards for
incidental on-sale alcoholic beverage establishments, with the exception of proximity to
residential uses because residences will be located within 300 feet of the use; however,
the applicant is requesting a modification to the location standards, as specified within
PMC Section 17.92.070.D.3.c, to reduce the residential distance separation requirement
from 300 feet to 26 feet. In addition, the project site is surrounded by commercial
businesses and residences that were approved in conjunction with the previous CUP for
alcohol sales at this location and the grocery store will provide an amenity for future
residents. Therefore, the location is appropriate for this type of use.

Operations

The grocery store will operate between 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. The applicant will
be required to comply with all Conditions of Approval, restrictions of the ABC license, ABC
regulations, and reapply for a new ABC license should the use of the premises qualify for
a different license type. The sale, display, storage, and on-site tasting of beer, wine, and
spirits will utilize less than three percent of the total floor area and will be incidental to the
primary grocery store use. Also, Conditions of Approval have been included within the
draft resolution to mitigate any potential impacts associated with alcohol sales that may

instructional tasting event, the instructional tasting event area will be separated from the
remainder of the premises by a wall, rope, cable, cord, chain, or other permanent or

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) Guidelines review pursuant to Section 15301 of the CEQA Guidelines, which
exempts licensing of existing uses with negligible expansion of the use. This proposed
project will establish beer, wine, and distilled spirits sales and host tasting events within
a grocery store, which is expected to be a negligible expansion of the use. No expansion
or exterior modifications of the building or parking area are proposed as part of this
application.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicants are requesting a two-year time extension for a previously approved 21-
acre commercial and residential development located at the northwest corner of
Rancho Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West. The project consists of a 308-unit
apartment complex, 36-unit townhome development, and approximately 47,000 square
feet of retail/commercial development on a vacant site. The commercial complex is
located at the northwest corner of 15th Street West and Rancho Vista Boulevard within
the southern portion of the site. The apartment complex is located on the northern portion
of the site and the townhomes are located on the western portion of the site. No changes
to the site are proposed as part of this time extension application. LaTerra Development
is the applicant for the residential portion of the site and Sage Investco is the applicant
for the commercial portion.

BACKGROUND

The project was originally approved by the Planning Commission on July 11, 2019,
though Resolution No. PC-2019-027 for Planned Development (PD) 19-001,
Tentative Tract Map (TTM) 82636, Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 19-002, and
SPR 19-003 for the development of a mixed-use project. On August 6, 2019, the City
Council approved General Plan Amendment (GPA) 19-001 and Zone Change (ZC)
19-001 through Resolution No. CC-2019-068 in conjunction with the above approvals.
Following approval of the development, applications were approved by the Planning
Commission on May 13, 2021, through Resolution No. PC-2021-012 to phase the
subdivision of the site through TTM 82636 Major Modification No. 1. In addition, the
commercial portion of the project has been modified through Minor Modifications 19-075,
21-036, and 21-066, and the residential portion through Minor Modification 22-018.

GPA 19-001 and ZC 19-001 approved changes to the land use designation and zone to
accommodate the residential components of the project, PD 19-001 allowed flexibility of
development standards, TTM 82636 and TTM 82636 Major Modification approved the
subdivision and phasing of lots, and CUP 19-002 allowed the sale of beer and wine
(Alcoholic Beverage Control License Type 20 – Off-sale Beer and Wine) within a
proposed grocery store in the commercial component of the site.

PD 19-001 was approved for a period of five years, establishing an expiration date of
July 23, 2024. On March 2, 2022, the City Council adopted Urgency Ordinance U-1582
amending Palmdale Municipal Code Section 16.40.120 to increase the initial term of
tentative maps by one year for housing projects that were in effect on March 1, 2022, and
 Staff Report to the Planning Commission

that will expire before December 31, 2022. As such, the expiration date of TTM 82636
was extended until July 23, 2023, and CUP 19-002 and SPR 19-003 expired on
July 23, 2022.

Through the recent adoption of Palmdale 2045, a comprehensive General Plan Update,
the land use designation of this site has been changed to Mixed Use 2 (MU2). The
approved project is consistent with the intent of the MU2 designation; however, as a
complete, or substantially complete application was submitted prior to the
October 22, 2022, effective date of Palmdale 2045, this project will be evaluated based
on the previous land use designation, the planned development document, and any
applicable standards.

The proposed time extension application was submitted on June 8, 2022, and was
deemed incomplete. After resolution of completeness items, the application was deemed
complete on September 12, 2022, and scheduled for the November 10, 2022, Planning
Commission meeting. Subsequently, the applicant requested a continuance to the
December 8, 2022, Planning Commission meeting.

The project site is currently fenced off as development activity is on-going. The
commercial and residential components of the project are both in the process of procuring
grading and building permits; however, above ground construction has not yet
commenced.

Access/Circulation

Vehicular access to the site will be provided from four new driveways: one on
Rancho Vista Boulevard and three on 15th Street West. Right-turn lanes will be provided
at the north and south driveways on 15th Street West and the driveway on
Rancho Vista Boulevard. Vehicles exiting the site will be able to make right and left
turning movements out of the 15th Street West driveways and only right turning
movements out of the Rancho Vista Boulevard driveway.

In addition, two emergency access points are provided onto 15th Street West from the
apartment portion of the site for use by Los Angeles County Fire Department apparatus
only. These access drives will be clearly marked and are not intended to be open for
public vehicular ingress or egress to the site. No changes are proposed as part of this
time extension.

Pedestrian access will be provided into the site through the installation of sidewalks
adjacent to the project along all street frontages. In addition, pedestrian access, shaded
through the use of pergolas and landscaping, will be provided throughout the site and
include connections from the residential portions of the site to the commercial portion of
the site, as well as to surrounding development.

Elevations

The PD establishes design standards to ensure a cohesive design and compatible
architecture for both the residential and commercial portions of the site. The colors and
materials for the approved project have been modified through minor modifications;
however, no additional changes are proposed as part of this application.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

An Initial Study was prepared for the project in conjunction with original approval, and on
July 11, 2019, the Planning Commission adopted an MND finding that, with mitigation,

Modification No. 1 to address updated guidelines provided by the California Department
of Fish and Wildlife regarding the western Joshua tree. Staff review of the project has
determined that a subsequent or supplemental MND as described in California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Sections 15162, 15163 or 15164 of
CEQA Guidelines, is not required for the project because SPR 19-003 TE does not
propose significant revisions to the project, there are no significant changes in
circumstances and there is no new information of substantial importance that will involve
new significant environmental effects or increase the severity of previously identified
significant effects. The proposed project is a request for a two-year time extension of
SPR 19-003 to construct the previously approved mixed-use development and does not
propose any alterations to the approved plans.

 1.  INTRODUCTION
A.  Project Background

  The purpose of the Draft Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration is to
  evaluate if a project would have a significant impact on the environment. The
  Proposed Project is a mixed-use development consisting of multi-residential and
  commercial facilities on the vacant 20.55-acre property in the City of Palmdale.

  The Proposed Project area is located within the City of Palmdale which
  encompasses approximately 174 square miles. The City’s General Plan includes
  Land Use, Circulation, Environmental Resources, Public Services, Safety, Noise,
  Housing, Parks, Recreation and Trails, and Community Design Elements. The
  General Plan was adopted by the City Council on January 25, 1993. Section
  15150 of the CEQA Guidelines allows the incorporation by reference of
  documents that are generally available to the public. This Initial Study has been
  prepared utilizing information from the City’s General Plan, and other publicly
  available data. Documents used in the Initial Study are identified in Section 5 and
  are incorporated by reference.

 2.  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
A.  Project Location

  The Proposed Project site is a vacant parcel located at the northwest corner of
  Rancho Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West in the City of Palmdale. West
  Avenue O-12 (a private drive) is located to the north of the Proposed Project site,
  15th Street West is to the east, and Rancho Vista Boulevard is to the south. An
  existing residential tract borders the site on the west.

B.  Project Setting

  The General Plan land use designation of the Proposed Project site is CC
  (Community Commercial) and the property is zoned C-3 (General Commercial).
  Land uses surrounding the Proposed Project site include Regional Commercial
  (RC) to the east, and Single Family Residential (SFR-3) to the south and west.
  Zoning surrounding the Proposed Project site includes C-4 (Commercial Center)
  to the east, and Single Family Residential (R-1-7,000) to the south and west
  which designates a minimum lot size of 7,000 square feet. The properties to the
  north of the site are within Los Angeles County jurisdiction and according to the
  Los Angeles Planning and Zoning for Unincorporated Los Angeles County, the
  area north of the site is zoned for Heavy Agricultural (A-2).

  Antelope Valley Mall is located east of 15th Street West and the Proposed
  Project site. It consists of a large central retail center, with an entrance and
  parking lot adjacent to 15th Street West. Single-family homes are located south
  of the Proposed Project site across Rancho Vista Boulevard and immediately
  west of the Proposed Project site along Dover Drive. A block wall separates the
  houses along Dover Drive from the Proposed Project site. Homes south of
  Rancho Vista Boulevard also have a block wall that separates the homes from
  the sidewalk along the street. North of the Proposed Project are fenced
  residential properties. West Avenue O-12, along 15th Street West, is a private
  unpaved roadway.

C.  Project Components

  The Applicant proposes the construction of a mixed-use development including
  multi-family residential and commercial facilities on the vacant 20.55-acre
  property. The Proposed Project consists of a 308-unit apartment complex, 36-
  unit townhome development, and 43,200 square feet of retail/commercial
  development. The Proposed Project components are summarized below:

The apartment complex will be located on the northern portion of the site. The
commercial complex will be located at the northwest corner of 15th Street West
and Rancho Vista Boulevard within the southern portion of the project. The
townhome units will be located west of the commercial complex adjacent to the
existing residential tract on the western portion of the site. This would allow
connectivity and accessibility of the residents to retail and commercial
businesses.

The complex will consist of the following floor plans:

Apartments:

  • 462 square-feet up to 1,088 square feet

Townhomes:

Further details are provided on Figure 3: Site Plan. The perimeter of the
apartment complex and townhomes will include installation of a combination of
gates and walls separating the residential areas from the retail/commercial area
but would allow pedestrian connectivity between the areas. On-site amenities
such as play areas and swimming pools will be shared by residents of the
townhomes and apartments. Off-site improvements will include the addition of
curb, gutter, sidewalk and pavement widening along the frontage of 15th Street
West, including left-turn and right-turn pockets at the entrances to the apartments
and the commercial center. The improvements also include a center median and
a right turn lane at the entrance to the commercial center on Rancho Vista
Boulevard.

A Planned Development document will be prepared for the Proposed Project.
The Planned Development document will allow the Applicant to modify
development standards to provide flexibility and cohesiveness The Proposed
Project will also include a conditional use permit, site plan review, tentative tract
map, zone change, and general plan amendment for the development of a
mixed-use site. The current land use and zoning designation does not include a
residential component. The zone change and General Plan amendment would
allow residential facilities to be included on the site.

   Access

  Access to the apartments will be provided through a main gated entrance along
  15th Street West. There is also an Emergency Vehicle access point towards the
  north side of the complex on 15th Street East. The Apartments also have a
  second gated access into the complex from the commercial center. The
  Commercial Center will have three entrances, a main access and a service lane
  entrance on 15th Street West and a main access on Ranch Vista Boulevard. The
  Townhomes will have gated access from the commercial center drive from
  Rancho Vista Boulevard and access from the apartment complex.

  Project Construction

  Construction for the Proposed Project is anticipated to begin in Fall 2019. The
  proposed construction will occur in a single phase with the following estimated
  duration: apartments construction for 18 months, townhomes construction for 12
  months, and retail construction for 10 months, not including interior
  improvements. The commercial center is anticipated to be operational by late
  Spring 2020. The Proposed Project area will be graded prior to building
  construction. Construction activities are scheduled to occur Monday through
  Friday. Per the City of Palmdale Municipal Code, building construction hours will
  be restricted between the hours of 8:00 PM to 6:30 AM. Equipment to be used
  onsite includes excavators, earthmovers, frontend loaders, backhoes,
  compactors, cement mixers, water trucks, cranes, forklifts, and other typical
  construction equipment. Staging areas for the Proposed Project will be located
  onsite.

 D.  EVALUATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS

Each of the responses in the following environmental checklist considers the whole
action involved, including project-level, cumulative, on-site, off-site, indirect,
construction, and operational impacts. A brief explanation is provided for all answers
and supported by the information sources cited.

  1. A “No Impact” answer is adequately supported if the referenced information
  sources show that the impact simply does not apply to projects like the one
  involved (e.g., the project falls outside a fault rupture zone).

  2. A “Less Than Significant Impact” applies when the proposed project would
  not result in a substantial and adverse change in the environment. This
  impact level does not require mitigation measures.

  3. A “Less Than Significant Impact With Mitigation Incorporated” applies when
  the proposed project would not result in a substantial and adverse change in
  the environment after additional mitigation measures are applied.

  4. “Potentially Significant Impact” is appropriate if there is substantial evidence
  that an effect is significant. If there are one or more “Potentially Significant”
  entries when the determination is made, an EIR is required.

Project Impacts and Mitigation Measures

a)  Less Than Significant Impact. The City of Palmdale General Plan (City of
  Palmdale 1993) identifies open space, landscaped corridors, and viewsheds of
  the surrounding Angeles National Forest as providing visual enhancement and
  pleasure. Specific areas identified as containing aesthetically significant
  resources worthy of preserving include: Lamont Oddett Vista Point, Godde Hills
  Road, Bouquet Canyon Road, and Juniper Hills Road. The Proposed Project site
  is not in the vicinity of these identified aesthetic resources. Scenic vistas, or
  scenic viewsheds or backdrops as identified in the General Plan, refer to the
  significant ridgelines of the San Gabriel mountains, the Sierra Pelona range, and
  the Ritter and Portal Ridges that form the City’s skyline views. The Proposed
  Project is located within an urban and built-out environment and is not in the
  vicinity of any landscaped corridors or open space. Viewsheds of Angeles
  National Forest or the General Plan’s scenic viewsheds would not be significantly
  altered due to implementation of the Proposed Project. There are no parks or
  trails located nearby the Proposed Project where it would block any views of the
  ridgelines. A bus stop is located at the southern portion of the Proposed Project
  site along Rancho Vista Boulevard. However, the bus stop is facing south, and
  users’ views of the ridgelines will not be obstructed. Views of the mountains may
  be temporarily blocked while driving along Rancho Vista Boulevard but the
  intermittent blockage of views would not constitute a significant impact.
  Therefore, implementation of the Proposed Project would result in a less than
  significant impact associated with scenic vistas.

b)  No Impact. Currently, no officially designated or eligible state scenic highways

  17
   are near the Proposed Project site. The nearest designated or eligible state
  scenic highway is Interstate 210, approximately 25 miles southwest of the
  Proposed Project site (Caltrans 2011).

c)  Less Than Significant Impact. The General Plan land use designation of the
  Proposed Project site is CC (Community Commercial) and the site is zoned C-3
  (General Commercial). Land uses surrounding the Proposed Project site are
  within the unincorporated Los Angeles County jurisdiction areas to the north, RC
  (Regional Commercial) to the east, Single-Family Residential (SFR-3 [3.1-6
  du/ac]) to the south and west. Zoning surrounding the Proposed Project site
  include unincorporated Los Angeles County jurisdiction areas to the north, C-4
  (Commercial Center) to the east, and Single-Family Residential (R-1-7,000) to
  the south and west. The Community Commercial (CC) designation is intended for
  businesses providing retail and service uses which primarily serve the local
  market. Representative uses include restaurants, apparel stores, hardware
  stores, grocery markets, banks, offices, and similar uses. The Proposed Project
  will include a site plan review , zone change, and General Plan amendment for
  the development of a mixed-use site which would consist of residential and
  commercial uses.

  The presence of construction equipment and materials during the construction
  phase could result in the disturbance of the existing character of the site.
  Construction impacts could include fencing of the Proposed Project area,
  signage, lighting, and transporting of equipment. Once fully built, the Proposed
  Project would result in a permanent impact to the visual character of the
  Proposed Project area with the presence of the residences and commercial
  properties with the maximum height of 45 feet .

  The development of the Proposed Project will construct a live-work space by
  providing residents access to retail and commercial businesses within walking
  distance of their neighborhood. The construction of the Proposed Project would
  replace the vacant and disturbed lot and would utilize building materials that
  would complement the aesthetics of the existing residences, retail, and
  commercial buildings. Additionally, the Proposed Project would comply with
  Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Sections 17.86.010 and 17.87.050.H.2 which
  will require landscaping associated with the Proposed Project to maximize the
  aesthetic quality on site.

  While the Proposed Project would result in visual impacts during construction
  such as the presence of equipment, vehicles, and construction fencing around
  the site, these impacts would be short term in nature and limited to the
  construction phase only. In addition, the Proposed Project would include
  construction BMPs including but not limited to proper storage of equipment,
  project site maintenance and clean up, dust control measures, and limiting hours
  of construction within the hours mandated by the PMC in order to minimize any
  impacts regarding the visual character of the area.

  18
   Permanent impacts would include the presence of a new development on a
  currently vacant lot. The Proposed Project is located within an urbanized area
  and the surroundings are fully developed with residential and commercial
  buildings. The Proposed Project uses would be consistent with the General Plan
  with the approval of the proposed General Plan Amendment and the building
  height will be compatible with heights allowed within the surrounding area.
  According to PMC Section 17.16.020, primary structures are not to exceed 45
  feet for buildings in the C-3 (General Commercial) zone and R-3 (multiple-family
  residential) zone and 60 feet in the R-4 (high-density residential) zone.
  Additionally, there are no resources on site that hold scenic value. Therefore,
  implementation of the Proposed Project would result in a less than significant
  impact associated with visual character and scenic quality.

d)  Less Than Significant Impact. The Proposed Project will include temporary and
  permanent lighting to the Proposed Project area.

  During construction, the Proposed Project will include temporary construction
  lighting for areas requiring additional lighting such as confined spaces, and any
  digging. The Proposed Project will limit construction hours within the PMC
  requirement where construction activities are restricted between 8:00 PM to 6:30
  AM. Other additional lighting sources would come from vehicles and other large
  operating equipment. Once operational, permanent lighting sources will be from
  outdoor lighting necessary to ensure safety and vehicle lights.

  Lighting associated with the Proposed Project would be required to comply with
  PMC Section 17.86.030 which requires consistent illumination levels with the
  character and use of surrounding development; excessive illumination is not
  allowed. Additionally, exterior lighting would be required to be located and
  designed to minimize glare beyond the Proposed Project site; glare onto adjacent
  properties will be minimized by using downcast, cut-off type fixtures, as
  necessary, that are shielded and would direct the light towards specific areas
  requiring illumination. For areas that are located nearby residents, the lowest
  allowable lighting levels will be used.

  The Proposed Project also includes submittal of a Planned Development
  document, which provides specific development standards for this Project. The
  Planned Development document does not propose any changes to the lighting
  requirements as specified within PMC Section 17.86.030.  Therefore,
  implementation of the Proposed Project would result in a less than significant
  impact associated with light or glare.

Operational Emissions
Operational emissions consist of area sources (i.e., re-applying architectural
coatings, consumer products, and landscaping equipment), energy use (i.e.,
electricity and natural gas), mobile sources (e.g., commuting), stationary sources
(i.e., emergency generator), solid waste disposal, and water and wastewater use
(i.e., supplying and treating water and wastewater).

For area source architectural coating operations (i.e., re-applying coatings), VOC
emissions were calculated based on the assumption that the coatings would be
compliant with the VOC content limits of the AVAQMD’s Rule 1113.

Based on client input, the residential units will not have fireplaces or woodstoves
installed. In addition, the apartment buildings may have emergency generators
installed. To quantify the potential emissions, it was assumed that a 150-
horsepower natural gas-fired emergency generator would be installed. The
emissions from the emergency generator were conservatively estimated
assuming a maximum daily usage of 24 hours per day and a maximum annual
usage of 500 hours per year.

For mobile source emissions, the number of trips were calculated using the trip
rates (weekday trip rates) that were included in the traffic study and the Saturday
and Sunday trip rates that were provided by David Evans and Associates, Inc. As
stated previously in this report, the residential emissions were modeled using
three land use types in CalEEMod. The Institute of Transportation Engineers
(ITE) Trip Generation manual, 10th Edition combines the apartments and
condominiums/townhomes under the same Multifamily Housing land use type.
This is why the same trip rate is used for the individual residential land use types
in CalEEMod.

A Biological Resource Assessment and Native Vegetation Preservation Plan was
prepared for the Proposed Project by Mark Hagan, Wildlife Biologist, in February 2019
(Appendix B). The study was conducted to provide an assessment of biological
resources potentially occurring within, or utilizing the Proposed Project and also was
conducted to provide an estimated density and distribution of Joshua tree and California
juniper ecotone. A total of 12 line transects were walked on January 25, 2019 to
inventory biological resources.

Project Impacts and Mitigation Measures

a)  Less than Significant with Mitigation Incorporated.

  During the biological survey of the site, scattered litter, trash, shopping carts, and
  debris were observed within the Proposed Project area. In addition, off-highway
  vehicle tracks, dirt tracks, and a dirt road was observed. Foot and bike traffic was
  28
 observed, including an individual riding a bike within the area during the field
survey. A homeless encampment was observed within the study site; and
evidence of fire was observed.

The Proposed Project area was characteristic of a highly disturbed desert scrub
habitat. A total of 27 plant species were observed during the transect surveys.
California juniper was the dominant perennial species throughout the study area.
Red stemmed filaree (Erodium cicutarium) was the dominant annual species
within the study area. A total of 32 Joshua trees and 135 California juniper trees
were observed within the study area. No sensitive plant species were observed
within the study area.

A total of 17 wildlife species, or their sign were observed during the line transect
survey. No desert tortoises or their sign were observed during the field survey.
No burrowing owls or their sign were observed during the field survey. No
California ground squirrels (Citellus beecheyi) were observed on the study site.
Three inactive bird nests were observed within the study site, one in a Joshua
tree, two in silver cholla (Opuntia echinocarpa), and no nests were seen in the
California juniper trees.

The Mohave ground squirrel is a state listed threatened species; however the
Proposed Project area was not located within the geographic range of the
Mohave ground squirrel. The western limit of the geographic range of the
Mohave ground squirrel is currently thought to be Highway 14. The study area
appeared unsuitable to support Mohave ground squirrels, as human impacts on
the site are high and the site is adjacent to development on all four sides. No
mitigation for the Mohave ground squirrel is recommended.

Burrowing owls are considered a species of special concern by the California
Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW). While none were identified to be within
the Proposed Project area, the burrows of the California ground squirrel can
provide potential cover sites for burrowing owls and, as a result, may result in the
potential presence of burrowing owls.

The following mitigation measures are recommended regarding burrowing owls:

BIO-1:  A burrowing owl survey shall be accomplished within 30 days prior
  to any ground disturbing activities to ensure the absence of
  burrowing owl within the boundaries of disturbance. If the presence
  of burrowing owls is discovered, the California Department of Fish
  and Wildlife shall be consulted, and standard protocols shall be
  adhered to, prior to the occurrence of any ground disturbance.

The Proposed Project would not have a substantial adverse effect through
modification of habitats of candidate, sensitive, or special status species due to
the existing conditions of the Proposed Project area. The results of the Biological
Resource Assessment and Native Vegetation Preservation Plan (Appendix B)
indicated that there are no other state or federally listed species that are
  29

Historical Seismicity
The Palmdale area is in the seismically active southern California with at least
eight prominent major earthquakes historically affecting the area. These include
the 1812 Wrightwood, 1857 Fort Tejon, 1872 Owens Valley, 1952 Arvin‐
Tehachapi, 1971 San Fernando, 1992 Landers, 1994 Northridge, and 1999
Hector Mine earthquakes. Strong ground motions were experienced with
magnitudes ranging from approximately 6.5 to 7.9. Approximately 35 magnitude
5.5 or greater historic earthquakes have occurred within 60 miles of the
Proposed Project.

Design and construction of the new facilities would comply with all seismic-safety
development requirements, including the Title 24 standards of the current
California Building Code. Therefore, implementation of the Proposed Project
would result in a less than significant impact associated with strong seismic
ground shaking.

iii) Less Than Significant Impact.

Soil Liquefaction and Lateral Spreading
Liquefaction is the loss of soil strength from sudden shock (usually earthquake
shaking), causing the soil to become a fluid mass. Liquefaction describes a
phenomenon in which saturated soil loses shear strength and deforms as a result
of increased pore water pressure induced by strong ground shaking during an
earthquake. Dissipation of the excess pore pressures will produce volume
changes within the liquefied soil layer, which can cause settlement. Shear
strength reduction combined with inertial forces from the ground motion may also
result in lateral migration (lateral spreading). Factors known to influence
liquefaction include soil type, structure, grain size, relative density, confining
pressure, depth to groundwater, and the intensity and duration of ground
shaking. Soils most susceptible to liquefaction are saturated, loose sandy soils
and low plasticity clay and silt. In general, for the effects of liquefaction to be
manifested, groundwater levels must be within 50 feet of the ground surface and
the soils within the saturated zone must also be susceptible to liquefaction. The
project does not lie in a zone designated by California Geologic Survey for the
Ritter Ridge Quadrangle. Our exploration did not reveal a shallow groundwater
table or a perched water table. Our research of nearby water well data and
historic groundwater levels indicate both current and historic groundwater tables
are greater than 50 feet below the ground surface. Since groundwater tables are
greater than 50 feet below the existing ground surface (bgs), the estimated the
potential for liquefaction at the site is low.

Lateral spreading (lateral migration) is caused when a loose and saturated soil
layer is liquefied by a nearby earthquake of sufficient magnitude and a sloping
ground, free face conditions, or sufficient building/embankment stresses exist
near the site. Currently, these factors are not present at this site. The field and
laboratory testing indicate that the soils within 50 feet of the surface are not
  39
   subject to liquefaction. Therefore, lateral spreading at this site has a low potential
  (Appendix D).

  Because the Proposed Project site is not subject to liquefaction and contains low
  potential for lateral spreading, potential impacts associated with liquefaction or
  ground-failure is less than significant.

  The land use is as described in the ITE Land Use 820 (Shopping Center) with a
  composition to reflect the needs of the local area, encouraging visits to multiple
  locations in a single trip. Trip generation factors for the Multifamily Housing – Low
  Rise (ITE Land Use Category 220) and Shopping Center (ITE Land Use
  Category 820) were obtained from the Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE)
  Trip Generation manual, 10th Edition. The Focused Traffic Impact Analysis
  summarizes the estimated trip generation for the Proposed Project site during the

  anticipated to generate 3,685 primary daily trips, 186 primary trips during the AM
  peak, and 310 primary trips during the PM peak hours.

ambient growth and traffic generated by other area projects within the study area

  has a capacity of 12 mgd. The expected average wastewater flow from the

   1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

A Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) was prepared in 2019 for the construction of a
mixed-use development on a vacant 20.55-acre parcel located at the northwest corner of
Rancho Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West in the City of Palmdale (City). The 2019
Project, also known as the Strata West Palmdale Apartments and Strata Commons,
consisted of a 308-unit apartment complex, 36-unit townhome development, and 43,200
square feet of retail/commercial development. The 2019 Project site was zoned as
General Commercial (C-3), which allows commercial shopping centers with approval of a
site plan review application. In the City’s General Plan, the 2019 Project site was
designated as Community Commercial (CC), which is intended for businesses providing
retail and service uses that serve the local market (i.e. restaurants, apparel stores,
hardware stores, grocery markets, banks, offices, and similar uses). The 2019 Project
included a conditional use permit, site plan review, tentative tract map (TTM), zone
change, and general plan amendment for the development of a mixed-use site. The 2019
Project was approved by the City Council in August 2019.

The Proposed Project site is a vacant parcel located at the northwest corner of Rancho
Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West in the City of Palmdale. West Avenue O-12 (a
private drive) is located to the north of the Proposed Project site, 15th Street West is to
the east, and Rancho Vista Boulevard is to the south. An existing residential tract borders
the site on the west. Existing conditions have not changed significantly from the previous
2019 analysis.

On September 22, 2020 the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) accepted
the petition to list the western Joshua tree (Yucca brevifolia) as threatened or endangered
under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA). In accepting the petition, the
western Joshua tree was listed as a candidate species, defined by Section 2068 of the
Fish and Game Code, and is fully protected under CESA effective October 9, 2020 (CFGC
2020b). According to the Biological Resource Assessment and Native Vegetation
Preservation Plan prepared for the 2019 Project, a total of 32 western Joshua trees were
observed on the site (Hagan 2019). The Proposed Project must comply with both the
Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) in relation to the western Joshua trees.

Coyne Development (Applicant) proposes to transplant and remove a portion of the 32
western Joshua trees in compliance with the required permits for the approved project
and per Section 14.04 of the PMC. In addition, CDFW is a Responsible Agency under
CEQA and the Applicant must apply for an Incidental Take Permit from CDFW and pay
mitigation fees to CDFW for the take of western Joshua trees. The Proposed Project must
also comply with the PMC during the removal of western Joshua trees.

Since the approval of the 2019 Project, the following updates to the project are proposed
(Proposed Project):

  •  The proposed TTM and construction activities are proposed to occur in phases.
  •  The Proposed Project must comply with regulations for the western Joshua
   tree.

  3. SUMMARY

Article 11, Section 15162 of the CEQA Guidelines state that when an environmental
impact report (EIR) or negative declaration has been certified and adopted, no
subsequent document shall be prepared unless the lead agency determines that the
changes proposed would require major revisions to the certified environmental document,
would result in new and significant environmental effects, and/or new changes would
result in the increase in the severity of a previously identified significant effect. The
Proposed Project does not meet the criteria identified in Section 15162 of the CEQA
Guidelines based on the following:

Condition 1:

  ▪  Substantial changes in the project requires major revision to the previously
  prepared Initial Study due to the involvement of new significant environmental
  effects or substantial increase in the severity of previously identified effects;

The location of the Proposed Project site has been previously analyzed in the 2019
Project MND for the development of a 308-unit apartment complex, 36-unit townhome
development, and 43,200 square feet of retail/commercial development on the 20.55-acre
property. The site plan and development footprint of the Proposed Project would remain
the same as the site plan and development footprint previously analyzed by the 2019
Project MND. Additionally, proposed uses would be consistent with the current land use
designations. The current site conditions remain consistent with what was analyzed in the
previously prepared 2019 Project MND. With the proposed phasing of the TTM,
construction of the Proposed Project would occur in three phases instead of on phase as
previously proposed. Phasing the Proposed Project would add approximately two to four
months to the construction timeline; however, this extension would not be significant
enough to result in increased or new environmental effects nor is the length of
construction an environmental impact.

Based on the updated guidelines provided by CDFW regarding the western Joshua tree,
the Proposed Project would result in take of a recently listed candidate species under
CESA, the western Joshua tree. Compliance with the CDFW guidelines would not result
in substantial changes for the Proposed Project and would not require major revisions as
this information was not previously known during the preparation of the 2019 Project
 MND. Furthermore, attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and payment of CDFW
mitigation fees would ensure a less than significant impact to western Joshua tree in
addition to complying with the City’s existing Joshua tree ordinance. The biological
impacts remain consistent with what was analyzed in 2019 and the Proposed Project
would not result in new or significant impacts. No new impacts would be introduced by
the Proposed Project that require major revision to the 2019 Project MND.

Condition 2:

  ▪  Substantial changes occur with respect to the circumstances under which the
  project is undertaken which will require major revisions of the previous EIR or
  Negative Declaration due to the involvement of new significant environmental
  effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant
  effects;

Although the Proposed Project would result in take of a recently listed candidate species
under CESA, the western Joshua tree, attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and
payment of CDFW mitigation fees does not require major revisions to the 2019 Project
MND as it does not introduce new impacts or increase the severity of previously identified
effects. Attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and payment of CDFW mitigation fees
would ensure a less than significant impact to western Joshua tree in addition to
complying with the City’s existing Joshua tree ordinance. Therefore, the biological
impacts remain consistent with what was analyzed in 2019.

Phasing the Proposed Project would add approximately two to four months to the
construction timeline; however, this extension would not be significant enough to result in
increased or new environmental effects. Moreover, the Proposed Project would maintain
the same site plan development footprint as the 2019 Project, and conditions on the
Project site have not changed significantly. The proposed uses will also be the same as
what was previously analyzed, including the land use designations.

The Proposed Project will not require major revisions due to the involvement of new
significant environmental effects, or a substantial increase in the severity or previously
identified effects.

Condition 3

  ▪  New information of substantial importance, which was not known and could have
  not been known that shows a project will have one or more significant effects not
  discussed in the previous Initial Study; significant effects previously examined will
  be more severe; mitigation measures found not to be feasible will be feasible and
  substantially reduce significant effects; mitigation measures are considerably
  different from those analyzed in the previous Initial Study but the Applicant declines
  to adopt the measure.

New information, which was not known and could have not been known, has been brought
 to light following approval of the 2019 Project: the western Joshua tree was listed as a
candidate species under CESA. However, as described in the Biological Letter (Appendix
A), the listing of the western Joshua tree will not result in any significant effects not
previously discussed in the Initial Study with attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and
payment of CDFW mitigation fees. Furthermore, compliance with the CDFW guidelines
and the City’s existing Joshua tree ordinance ensures a less than significant impact to
western Joshua tree.

The Proposed Project proposes the construction to occur in phases. The additional two
to four months would not result in new significant effects. There is no other new
information of substantial importance because the vacant 20.55-acre parcel was
previously analyzed for the development of a mixed-use facility with the same site plan
and development footprint as the Proposed Project. Existing conditions have not changed
significantly from that previous analysis. As previously discussed, 32 western Joshua
trees are located on the Project site, some of which will be transplanted. The proposed
uses will also be the same as what was previously analyzed, including the land use
designations. The Proposed Project will not result in more significant impacts and
mitigation measures remain feasible, adoptable, and will reduce any impacts to less than
significant.
